headline: Ariane 6 flight VA271 with Amazon Leo satellites moved to today
audio_script:
Good morning. It is Tuesday, the twenty-fourth of November, and this is the Sovereign Space ATLAS briefing. Europe's Ariane 6 is due to launch today with Amazon satellites after a one-day delay. NATO's chief has said space is part of the alliance's defence pledge. And Russia's military says it has destroyed Starlink stations used by Ukrainian forces.

Arianespace has moved the launch of Ariane 6 flight VA271 from the twenty-third of November to today. The window opens at 10:45 and closes at 11:14 UTC. Arianespace's notice of the fourteenth of October said the rocket would carry 36 Amazon Leo satellites. It is the tenth Ariane 6 launch. No reason for the delay has been published, and the result is not yet known. The cause of the Vulcan failure of the fifteenth of November, with 40 Amazon satellites, is also still unpublished.

In Europe, the European Space Agency has released the first images of the asteroid Dimorphos taken by its Hera spacecraft since the impact on it. The agency streamed the release on the nineteenth of November. The vote of the tenth of November has no published outcome, and the MaiaSpace contract remains unsigned. The European Commission has recommended raising its competition fund five times. The next date is Rome on the fifteenth of December.

In Central and Eastern Europe, NATO's chief said on the twenty-first of November that allies stand with Poland after a Russian airspace breach. On the twenty-third he said space is part of the alliance's defence pledge, as claims circulate that Russia is readying a nuclear satellite. The sources we hold give no technical detail on that claim. No date has been set for any NATO step on space.

In the Nordics, Sweden's space agency has set its next Rymddagen for the eighteenth of February, twenty twenty-seven. Norway signed a joint declaration on the European Union's ISOS program for in-orbit satellite maintenance on the tenth of June. The Swedish date is the next one on the calendar.

In France, Airbus said on the ninth of November that it will deliver IRIS, France's next-generation military Earth observation satellites. The release held here gives no value or delivery date. Portugal's Azores launch step stands as filed.

In Russia, the military says it destroyed 149 drone control points and several Starlink stations used by Ukrainian forces. That is the Russian military's own claim, issued on the twenty-fourth of November. SpaceX has made no statement, and the mid twenty twenty-seven hope for Ukrainian access is unchanged. In Armenia, a protocol signed with Iran on technological cooperation covers space, logistics and postal services.

In Türkiye, trade press says a new microsatellite will launch in twenty twenty-eight. No operator or budget is given. The Turkic states' joint satellite is still set for twenty twenty-seven, and the budget proposal of nine billion lira for twenty twenty-seven stands without a split. In Algeria, the space agency has marked ten years of Alsat-2B in orbit.

In Australia, Sunburnt Space announced on the twenty-third of November its largest rocket yet, for a launch in twenty twenty-seven. Specifications are not in our material. In Japan, the H3 transition stands as filed from the JAXA release of the twentieth of November, with schedule and operator unknown.

In Mexico, local trade press is analysing the national space program for twenty twenty-six to twenty thirty. A plan of 540 million pesos for four security and climate satellites was reported in March. No new decision is dated. In the United States, Artemis proposals are due on the eighth of December.

What we are tracking this week: the result of Ariane 6 flight VA271 today, the cause of the Vulcan failure, and any SpaceX statement on Starshield. What we are tracking this month: Artemis proposals due on the eighth of December, and the outcome of the tenth of November vote ahead of Rome on the fifteenth of December. Heads-up dates are today, the eighth of December, the fifteenth of December, and the eighteenth of February for Rymddagen. That is the briefing for Tuesday, the twenty-fourth of November.
